validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, independently confirmed, correctly classified. This row is the 'Acadian Haynesville Extension' segment of Enterprise Products' Acadian Gas Pipeline System -- an intrastate gas trunkline linking Haynesville shale production in northwest Louisiana to Acadian's south Louisiana network and nine interstate pipelines (Florida Gas, Texas Eastern, Transco, Sonat, Columbia Gulf, Trunkline, ANR, Tennessee Gas, Texas Gas). Confirmed via: (1) Oil & Gas Journal, 'Enterprise, Duncan to expand Acadian gas line into Haynesville shale', Oct. 28, 2009 -- names the project 'the Haynesville Extension' explicitly, states initial scope of 249 mi / 30-36in / 1.4 bcfd, in-service target Sept. 2011; (2) Enterprise Products Partners LP, Investor Presentation filed with SEC, Oct. 2010 -- states 'Haynesville Extension pipeline project ... 270-mile, 42"/36" pipeline with approximately 1.8 Bcf/d of capacity; can be expanded to 2.1 Bcf/d ... Total cost of approximately $1.56 billion ... Expected in service September 2011'; (3) Enterprise Products' own 'Our History' page -- 2011 entry: 'Commercial operations on the Haynesville Extension of our Acadian Gas system began in November [2011]. This provides producers in Louisiana's Haynesville and Bossier Shale plays with access to 1.8 Bcf/d of incremental natural gas takeaway capacity'; (4) OGJ, 'EPP completes 400-MMcfd Acadian Haynesville Extension expansion', May 31, 2023, and Enterprise's own Businesswire release of the same date (read via Wayback after a live-site 403/timeout) -- both confirm the pipeline is still operating in 2023 and describe a compression expansion. Two independent origins (OGJ trade press vs. Enterprise/SEC self-disclosure) corroborate existence, timeline, and physical description; classification as 'transmission' (not gathering/distribution) is correct given the large diameter (30-42in), multi-hundred-mile length, and role connecting a producing basin to interstate trunklines and LNG-market industrial customers -- a textbook large intrastate transmission trunk, not a wellhead gathering system. DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate of any roster row. It IS however closely related to P3283 ('Acadian Gas Pipeline System', len=83.0, cap=1000.00) -- see cross_row_leads: strong evidence P3283 is Enterprise's separate 'Gillis Lateral' project (an 80-83-mile, 1 Bcf/d lateral built 2019-2021 off the Haynesville Extension mainline), a physically distinct pipeline, not a double-count of this row. Opened 8 of the 15 harvested wiki citations for this page (Enterprise 'Our History', the SEC investor presentation, LNGprime 2021, PGJ 2019 via Wayback, OGJ 2009, OGJ 2023, Businesswire 2023 via Wayback, Aegis Hedging 2021); did not open: the EIA naturalgas/data.php navigation page (per scope guidance, not a citable value ref), Enterprise's interactive system-map and its generic 'Natural Gas Pipelines & Services' landing page (superseded by the richer 'Our History' page's text), two Enterprise career/job-posting URLs (irrelevant to pipeline specs), and mergr.com + the bit.ly 2000 press-release link (both describe the 2000 Shell-to-Enterprise acquisition of the PARENT Acadian system, predating this segment's 2009 proposal by nearly a decade -- not evidence for this row).

But it has since been expanded TWICE, both before the sheet's own LastUpdated of 2023-08-18: (a) Dec. 2021 -- Enterprise's Gillis Lateral project raised capacity from 1.8 to 2.1 Bcf/d via added horsepower at the Mansfield compressor station (confirmed independently by LNGprime, Dec. 16 2021; PGJ, Sept. 20 2019 [via Wayback, live URL 404s]; Aegis Hedging, 2021; and Enterprise's own 'Our History' page); (b) May 31, 2023 -- a further 400 MMcf/d compression-only expansion raised capacity from 2.1 to 2.5 Bcf/d (confirmed independently by OGJ, 'EPP completes 400-MMcfd Acadian Haynesville Extension expansion', May 31 2023, and Enterprise's own Businesswire release of the same date [read via Wayback], both explicit: 'increasing total natural gas transportation capacity on the Acadian Haynesville Extension from approximately 2.1 ... to 2.5 Bcf/d'). Two independent origins (OGJ trade press vs. Enterprise corporate press release) agree on 2.5 Bcf/d as of May 2023 -- three months before this row's LastUpdated. This is a material disagreement per the corroboration rule and is NOT being silently passed or auto-applied; flagging for Update. Note this expansion added compression only, no new pipe, so it does not change Length/Diameter.

This is a physically DISTINCT lateral pipeline built 2019-2021, not a duplicate of P5709 (the original 2009-2011 Haynesville Extension mainline) -- recommend the orchestrator route these sourced facts (83 mi, 1000 MMcf/d, Alexandria LA -> Gillis LA, in-service Dec. 2021, cost not stated) to P3283's own row for ref-fills if its worklist has open MISSING_VALUE/MISSING_REF units.
